text_blocks.snippet: Constitutional symptoms are general, non-specific signs and symptoms that affect the overall well-being of an individual. They are not typically associated with a specific organ system or disease.
snippet_highlighted_words: general, non-specific signs and symptoms that affect the overall well-being of an individual

text_blocks.snippet: Fatigue, Fever, Weight loss, Malaise, Chills, Night sweats, Muscle aches, Joint pain, Headache, and Anorexia (loss of appetite).

Constitutional symptoms can be caused by a wide range of underlying conditions, including infections, autoimmune disorders, cancers, and chronic diseases. They may also be a sign of an underlying psychological issue or stress.
If you experience any constitutional symptoms, it is important to consult a healthcare professional to determine the underlying cause and receive appropriate treatment.
